page: Amazon Web Services f2.12xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 7R13 processor operating at 3.4 GHz. It features 24 physical cores and 48 vCPUs with hyperthreading enabled. The memory configuration consists of 512.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, providing 10.67 GB of memory per core. Local storage is provided via a 1880 GB NVMe SSD, and the network interface delivers a baseline bandwidth of 25 Gbps. The instance runs on the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark data indicates strong performance in several compute-heavy areas. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests both rank in the top 25%, as does the PassMark CPU score and PassMark encryption test. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, Geekbench ray tracing, and Geekbench image processing also demonstrate strong performance. However, memory bandwidth tests for both small cached blocks and large uncached blocks fall within the average range.

While the server handles standard compute tasks and multi-threaded decompression efficiently, it exhibits performance limitations for specific workloads. LLM inference speed for text generation using a large 70B model is poor, falling into the bottom 10%, though prompt processing for the same model remains average. The server is suited for memory-intensive applications, database operations, and workloads requiring local NVMe storage, but is less optimal for large-scale LLM text generation.
